stage: T0 -- run before any EM, no LLM and no encoder

criteria.T0b_cross_table_addr_collision: at most half of S2 (hitab <= .0565, aitqa <= .1345)
criteria.T5_token_growth: <= +0.25 (a prediction, but measurable at T0 and reported here)

why: S2h (PREREG 3 as written) passes T0a and T0b on every corpus but costs +190% to +744% tokens per cell, 8x over the T5 cap. On HiTab it is 42.66 tok/cell, MORE than the title scheme S3 it is meant to replace (38.2). Registering it would re-run the S2t capacity confound an order of magnitude larger.

The exclusion rule of 3 is what makes it expensive AND what makes the term per-cell instead of per-table: in a table whose header forest has many roots, a cell under one root carries all the others. A term that differs cell to cell cannot narrow retrieval to a table, which is the one share (+.069) the prereg exists to buy.

Every single-label pick rule that fits under the cap cuts HiTab by two thirds (11.31% -> 3.7%) but never halves AIT-QA (best 14.6% against a 13.45% bar) or RealHiTBench (best 19.1% against 15.2%). Every rule that halves them blows the cap. The frontier does not contain a passing point.

AIT-QA resists for a structural reason, not a tuning one: its cross-table collisions run between NEAR-DUPLICATE TABLES -- same company, same metrics, overlapping fiscal years. tab-12 and tab-112 are 175 cells each and share 75 byte-identical addresses. 97 table pairs are involved and the top 10 carry 50.9% of the colliding addresses. Two tables with the same header tree get the same header-derived term by construction, so this share is unreachable by the whole family of PREREG 3 schemes, not by one pick rule. Making the label near-unique does not help: row+col slots give 102/113 distinct labels and still leave 13.6%.

best_under_cap.rule: rare,short:one -- the table's rarest root, ties to the shorter label, on every cell of the table

note_on_the_gate_itself: T0b tests COLLISION, but PREREG 2 already established that collision reduction alone does not buy EM -- S2t drove HiTab's cross-table collision to 0.00% and still lost .032 on AIT-QA. The open question there is the NARROWING share, which depends on a query matching the term, not on whether two addresses are identical. A re-registration should say which of the two it is gating on; this verdict reports T0 as written and does not relax it.
